TechieDesk for macOS — installing an UNSIGNED build
====================================================

This build is not signed with an Apple Developer ID and is not notarized
(REQ-FN-038c — the owner has no Apple Developer identity). Everything in the
app works normally; what is missing is Apple's signature, and macOS therefore
treats the app as coming from an unidentified developer.

INSTALL
-------
1. Drag TechieDesk.app onto the Applications folder in this window.

2. The first launch WILL be refused. macOS shows either
     "TechieDesk.app is damaged and can't be opened"
   or
     "TechieDesk.app cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified"
   Neither means the download is corrupt — it means the app is unsigned and
   carries a quarantine flag from having been downloaded.

3. Remove the quarantine flag, once, in Terminal:

     xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/TechieDesk.app

   Then open the app normally. You will not need to repeat this.

   (Right-click -> Open sometimes works instead, but on recent macOS versions
   the "is damaged" variant cannot be bypassed that way — the xattr command is
   the reliable route.)

WHAT THIS COSTS YOU
-------------------
One feature is genuinely degraded, not just cosmetically:

  * Sessions and provider API keys are NOT stored in the macOS Keychain.
    Mac Catalyst refuses Keychain access to a build without a
    provisioning-profile-backed entitlement (errSecMissingEntitlement). The app
    detects this at startup, logs it, and falls back to memory-only for the
    run. Nothing sensitive is written to a file instead — the secret simply
    does not survive a restart, so you sign in again after quitting.

    This is REQ-FN-039's known gap and it disappears the moment the app is
    signed; the code needs no change.

Everything else — local RAG, workspaces, ingestion, Qdrant administration,
the data directory under ~/Library/Application Support/TechieDesk — is
unaffected.

UNINSTALL
---------
Delete /Applications/TechieDesk.app. Your data stays at
~/Library/Application Support/TechieDesk until you delete that too.
